title: Importance of Uniform Drainage Pipe Slope
description: Maintaining consistent pitch on horizontal drainage pipes is critical for self-scouring velocity. If the slope is too shallow, water moves too slowly, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle on the bottom of the pipe and build up over time. Conversely, an excessive pitch can allow liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solid waste behind. Plumbing codes specify mandatory minimum slope requirements based on pipe diameter. Ensuring proper pipe support with rigid hangers prevents sagging, eliminates low spots, and guarantees reliable waste transportation throughout the building's drainage network.

Importance of Uniform Drainage Pipe Slope

Maintaining consistent pitch on horizontal drainage pipes is critical for self-scouring velocity. If the slope is too shallow, water moves too slowly, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle on the bottom of the pipe and build up over time. Conversely, an excessive pitch can allow liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solid waste behind. Plumbing codes specify mandatory minimum slope requirements based on pipe diameter. Ensuring proper pipe support with rigid hangers prevents sagging, eliminates low spots, and guarantees reliable waste transportation throughout the building's drainage network.
